title: Urine microalbumin
what: This is a urine test. It looks for very small amounts of a protein called albumin, which a routine test does not pick up.
why: Once a year with diabetes or high blood pressure, to catch early strain on the kidneys.
duration: collecting takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If you have a cold, a fever, or a urinary infection right now
If you had a hard workout the day before
If you have your period now
What blood pressure and sugar medicines you take

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No hard workouts and no alcohol. Better not to eat a lot of meat.

prepare.title: Collecting
prepare.text: Usually a morning sample, sometimes a 24-hour collection. Ask the lab which one you need.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

steps: In the morning, wash with warm water, no soap
Pee the first few seconds into the toilet
Catch the middle part in a sterile container
Close the lid and take it to the lab within 1 to 2 hours
after: Results usually come in 1 to 2 days
If the result is high, the doctor usually asks you to repeat the test

faq.q: If albumin is high, does that mean my kidneys are sick?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It can rise for a short time after exercise or with a fever. That is why the test is repeated.

faq.q: How often should I have it with diabetes?
faq.a: Usually once a year. Your doctor will tell you more exactly.

reminders.text: Urine microalbumin test tomorrow. Today, no hard workouts and no alcohol.
